content.title: About
content.content: Lettuce (Lactuca sativa) is an annual herb cultivated for its crisp leaves. Green leaf lettuce is eaten raw in salads, sandwiches, and wraps. It has a mild, slightly bitter flavor and a high water content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lettuce belongs to the Asteraceae family and is a close relative of endive and romaine.
There are over 100 lettuce varieties differing in leaf shape, color, and texture.
Leafy lettuce is composed of about 95 % water.
Lettuce was known in ancient Egypt, where it was grown in specially irrigated gardens.
In Japan, the ‘batavo’ varieties are prized for their subtle bitterness and used in traditional dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Lettuce provides a high amount of vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate supports cell division and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: One cup of shredded lettuce contains fewer than 15 kcal, making it ideal for weight management.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: The leaves are rich in carotenoids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw lettuce can harbor Salmonella or E. coli, so thorough washing is essential.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional lettuce may contain chemical residues; choose organic or wash well.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of people may experience lettuce allergy, resulting in itching or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lettuce is eaten raw: in salads, sandwiches, wraps, smoothies, or as a side. Lightly drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, add salt and herbs for flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leaf lettuce in the refrigerator in a bag with a small amount of moisture or in a container lined with a paper towel. Use within 3–5 days. Discard any leaves that turn yellow or become slimy.
